---
title: "Project STAR: 79 schools"
subtitle: "Catalog A-01 and A-02"
description: "The Tennessee STAR class-size experiment, school by school: posterior effects under five priors on alpha barely move, while the implied number of clusters and the dominance of one cluster change a lot."
toc: false
---

Project STAR randomised pupils to small and regular classes within 79 Tennessee schools. The
paper fits the Dirichlet process mixture to the 79 school-level effects under five priors on
alpha. Switch the prior below: the schools hardly move.

```{=html}
<div id="w-star-cat" class="dpx-host column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/unit-caterpillar.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/app-prior-strip.js"></script>
```

- **The effects are stable.** From Vague to the Dual-Anchor prior the school means move by
  about .009 in root mean square, and never by more than .05; the same three schools have
  intervals that exclude zero.
- **Shift arrows** draw each school's move from its Vague posterior mean. At true scale they
  are nearly invisible; "draw shifts 10x longer" makes them visible and says so.

## The number of clusters does depend on the prior

The same five priors imply very different beliefs about K_79, the number of fitted components
among the 79 schools, and the data do not wash that out. The selector below follows the one
above.

```{=html}
<div id="w-star-strip" class="dpx-host column-page"></div>
<script>
  (function () {
    var q = new URLSearchParams(location.search), cat, strip;
    var specCat = { app: "star", onPrior: function (p) { if (strip) strip.update({ prior: p }); } };
    var specStrip = { app: "star", onPrior: function (p) { cat.update({ prior: p }); } };
    if (q.get("preset")) { specCat.preset = q.get("preset"); specStrip.preset = q.get("preset"); }
    cat = DPX["unit-caterpillar"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("w-star-cat"), specCat);
    strip = DPX["app-prior-strip"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("w-star-strip"), specStrip);
    window.__dpxStarCat = cat; window.__dpxStarStrip = strip;
  })();
</script>
```

- **The prior on K_79.** Vague expects 4.61 clusters (90% interval [1, 11]) with Pr(W_SB > .5)
  = .591; the Dual-Anchor prior (lambda = .20) expects 6.24 [3, 10] with .385; the hard bound
  is nearly a point mass at alpha = 2 (a above 3 million), with 7.93 and .250.
- **What the data leave.** The posterior E(K | data) goes from 1.96 under Vague to 4.47 under
  the Dual-Anchor prior, and the chance of a single cluster for all 79 schools from .560 to
  .064. The largest observed share falls from .920 to .724. These posterior numbers come from
  the replication package; only the prior side is computed here.
